questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why languages are dying out
How to learn Japanese quickly
Why British people don't learn languages as much as others do
Reasons to learn a language, and a useful tip
questions.why: They discuss the benefits of learning a language and Professor Webb's advice on which words to learn first.

questions.q: What is Neil's main tip for learning a language?
options: Practise a lot and don't be afraid of mistakes
Learn all the grammar first
Only study with a teacher
Live in the country where the language is spoken for a year
questions.why: Neil says 'practise, practise, practise – and don't be afraid of making mistakes'.

questions.q: According to a British Council survey, how many Britons made learning a language a New Year's resolution for 2018?
options: About half
About one in five
About one in ten
Almost everyone
questions.why: Neil says it was a new year's resolution for about one in five Britons in 2018.

questions.q: What did a study of people who speak one or two languages suggest?
options: Bilingual people earn more
Children always learn new languages much faster than adults do
Speaking two languages can slow the brain's decline
Learning two languages at once is confusing
questions.why: Neil says speaking two languages 'can help slow down the brain's decline with age'.

questions.q: According to Neil, what makes a second language easier to learn?
options: Being similar to your own language and culture
Having a very small vocabulary
Being spoken in many different countries around the world
Having a simple writing system
questions.why: He says the closer the language is to your native tongue and culture, the easier it will be.

questions.q: What did the study in Taiwan show, according to Professor Stuart Webb?
options: Most students learned more than 3,000 new words every single year
Students knew only the most common words
Students learned faster than expected
After nine years, half hadn't learned the top 1,000 words
questions.why: He says after nine years about half the students had failed to learn the most frequent 1,000 words.

questions.q: What does Professor Webb recommend learning first in English?
options: The 3,000 most difficult words
Words for travelling
The 800 most frequent word forms
Words with the most syllables
questions.why: He suggests learning 'the 800 most frequent lemmas' first.

options: Because they are the easiest to spell
They cover about 75% of English and give a foundation
Because they are used in exams
Because other, less frequent words are not important at all
questions.why: He says they account for about 75 per cent of English and provide the foundation for other words.
